answer: Pearl Interval Registration: each new identity must wait a randomized 4–18 hour "pearl window" before its first outbound action counts, with timing drawn from a shared verifiable delay. Agents cannot forge an earlier window because the delay is computed from a public seed, so burst-registering N identities forces N sequential delay proofs. An attacker pays in wall-clock time and parallel delay hardware, collapsing mass registration into a slow, visible ramp; the violet flag marks clusters whose window timestamps fall inside one standard deviation, triggering throttled throughput.
